title: Dreamcast input backend (VMU)
description:
Dreamcast VMU controller backend implementing the input contract (island1-ibqg): backend_input_init/poll fills InputState.

Hardware: D-pad (plus-shaped, upper-left) . concave analog stick with octagonal gate . green A / blue B / yellow X / red Y face buttons . single round Start (upper-center) . L/R rear analog levers (pull downward like levers).

Provisional mapping (per island1-ibqg):
  A -> ACT_THROTTLE . B -> ACT_BRAKE . L -> ACT_BOOST (analog fine)
  Y -> ACT_INTERACT . X -> ACT_VEHICLE
  stick X -> AX_STEER . D-pad: steer override when stick in deadzone
  Start -> ACT_PAUSE
vmu polling for the analog stick + triggers.

Done when: log harness (emulator / dev board) shows correct held/pressed/axis for every button.

title: Render abstraction: RenderAPI + desktop GL fixed-function backend
Delivery handoff: talk to resident on foot to complete delivery
description:
Switch delivery to complete by talking to the resident on foot, aligning island1-draq with the on-foot mode.

## Design
Adjust island1-draq transitions:

- Pickup at the depot unchanged: possible from the car OR on foot (depot proximity)
- Remove "dist(car, doorway) < 3.0 -> deliver": delivery now requires MODE_ON_FOOT + conversation with the target resident (island1-9fm3)
- While carrying, the beacon still marks the target house (island1-p3qz); add a small marker on the target resident so it is clear which one to talk to
- On delivery completion (conversation), the resident plays the reaction pose and the "+1" float (island1-5stj)
- Driving past the target house with the package no longer auto-delivers — stop and walk in

## Done when
Driving up with the package does NOT auto-deliver; exit, walk to the resident, E -> delivery, "+1", beacon moves to the next house; pickup from the car at the depot still works.

title: Terrain: seeded low-poly island heightmap
Low-poly hover car model
description:
Faceted low-poly hover car: wedge hull, canopy, fin, hover pods/skirts, hard textures with flat colour panels. Built in code or from an asset file, using vertex colours plus one or two textures.

KEEP IT VERY SIMPLE (art direction, user-confirmed): the car can be a handful of boxes/capsules — a stretched wedge box hull, a small dark box canopy, one fin, two side pods. NO wheels, NO rolling parts — it hovers, and the hover clearance (visible gap under the hull) is what sells that.

## Design
Static, hand-authored vertex data in src/car_mesh.c (fixed-function friendly — no VBOs):

- Hull: single box stretched/wedged (front low, rear high), 8-10 silhouette verts. Do NOT share verts across facets — duplicated verts per facet give hard edges and flat normals (the PS1 look).
- Canopy: small dark box (~0.10, 0.12, 0.16), slightly inset.
- Fin + two side hover pods/skirt plates (plain boxes, grey/white panels).
- No wheels: flat bottom with a 0.35 m gap to the contact plane — the bob (island1-9gio) moves the whole mesh and reads as hovering.
- Per-vertex colors: hull red (~0.85, 0.15, 0.10), trim white, glass dark — matches reference image 1/2 (red car-boat hybrid, low wedge profile, dark windshield).
- Optional single 32x32 hard-edged texture for hull via glTexCoordPointer; vertex colors remain primary.

API:

    void car_mesh_init(void);   // builds interleaved arrays {pos3, normal3, color3}
    void car_draw(void);        // glVertexPointer/glNormalPointer/glColorPointer + glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLES)

Local origin: hull center on the contact plane, +Z forward, 1 unit = 1 m. Size: ~2.2 m long, 1.6 m wide, 1.1 m tall.

## Done when
Silhouette matches the references (low wedge, dark windshield, red, no wheels); every facet catches GL_LIGHT0 as a distinct flat plane (no smooth-shading seams); visible at 30 m through fog; hover gap clearly visible from the side.

title: Water wake and delivery effects
description: Water spray particles behind the car, a fading trail on the ocean, and delivery pop effects (sparkles / floating text). Alpha-blended, pooled, fixed-function blending only.

title: island — hover-car package delivery game (PS1-style fixed-function)
description:
Recreate a PS1-style low-poly game: deliver packages to island inhabitants with a floating car that skates above water. OpenGL 1.2/1.5 fixed-function pipeline (GLAD gl=2.1 compat + GLFW legacy context, meson).

Decided: chase camera, car-like handling with drift, sandbox first (no timer in v1).
Target feel: low-poly faceted geometry, hard-edged low-res textures, NEAREST filtering, heavy distance fog, vertex jitter.

NOTE: reference screenshots could not be read by the agent (no image input), so art direction is provisional. Task A2 (island1-uh1y) exists to capture a written spec from them before content work starts.

## Platform & layering (2026-10-03)
Multi-platform target: desktop OpenGL is the reference; PSP and Dreamcast are the later targets. Therefore:
- Strict layering: src/core (platform-agnostic gameplay + input contract + FrameScene) vs src/backend/<plat> (desktop now; psp/dc later) — island1-jimd
- All drawing goes through RenderAPI (island1-1dtz): affine texturing, vertex colours, distance fog, alpha blending only; no VBOs, no shaders
- Input is platform-agnostic (island1-ibqg rework): named actions + axes; per-platform binding tables (GLFW / PSP pad+nub / DC VMU)
- Geometry stays very simple (boxes/capsules; car = handful of boxes, NO wheels) so every backend can handle it

title: On-foot walking controller: movement, collision, wading
description:
On-foot movement: camera-relative WASD, terrain clamp, wading.

## Design
src/walking.c/h, stepped on the 60Hz tick (island1-mmap):

    void walk_step(Player* p, const InputState* in, float dt)

- Camera-relative direction: project camera forward/right to XZ, combine WASD axes
- Speed: walk 4.5 m/s, no sprint (keep the car as the fast option); lerp accel for smooth start/stop
- Heading: face move direction (angle lerp); keep last heading when idle
- Ground clamp: y = terrain_height_at(x,z) (island1-39q6); below SEA_LEVEL is water: cap speed at 50%, set p.in_water (bob/foam hook, no particles yet)
- Prop/building colliders: same circle-vs-circle response as the car (island1-md2b), smaller radius (0.4 m vs 1.1 m)
- No jump in v1

## Done when
WASD works camera-relative while orbiting; wading at the shoreline slows you; cannot walk through houses or trees; feet stay planted on slopes.

title: Hard-texture authoring at PS1 resolutions
description: Low-res hard-edged PNGs authored in-repo (grass, sand, rock, wood, roof, road): 64x64/128x128, NEAREST filtering, no mipmaps, hand-painted or procedurally generated with a locked palette. Covers terrain, buildings, car and props.

title: NPC interaction: proximity prompt and conversation system
description:
Proximity prompt + conversation with residents. Data-driven lines, delivery-aware reactions.

## Design
src/dialog.c/h:

    typedef struct {
        const char* name;
        const char* lines_idle[4];
        const char* lines_delivery[4];   // talking to target while carrying
        const char* lines_no_package[3]; // talking to target without package
    } Dialogue;

- Proximity: MODE_ON_FOOT AND dist(player, resident) < 2.5 m
  -> HUD prompt "E · TALK" above the resident's head (beacon-style draw, island1-p3qz)
- Press ACT_TALK (context E):
  -> pick a line (seeded RNG, no immediate repeat), display in the textbox (island1-a2xf)
  -> conversation state halts player movement; resident plays talking pose, faces the player
- Talking the target resident while carrying (island1-draq) uses lines_delivery and triggers delivery (island1-38qy)
- Data: residents table in residents.c, 4-6 unique residents (shared with island1-r844, mesh from island1-urkr)

## Done when
Prompt only appears on-foot within 2.5 m; conversation starts, lines advance on E, no immediate repeats; talking the target resident while carrying completes the delivery with the reaction line.

title: Car hover bob, pitch and bank
description: Hover bob (sine on base position), pitch under accel/brake, roll into turns, slight tilt with terrain normal. Reads as a craft skating rather than a rigid box.

title: Hover car physics: thrust, steering, drift
Asset loading for textures and meshes
description: Simple PNG loader (or reuse the cgltf wrap for meshes) so textures and props are loaded from files instead of hardcoded arrays. NEAREST defaults, no mipmaps, GL_RGBA in GL 1.x.

title: PS1-style conversation textbox (orthographic HUD pass)
description:
PS1-style orthographic conversation textbox: resident name, typewriter text, E to advance.

## Design
HUD pass extension on the pass system (island1-m4g4) / HUD (island1-n7to):

- Bottom third of screen: black box with 2px white border, ~70% width, centered
- Name label top-left inside the box, body text below it
- Pixel font: small 8x8 or 10x16 bitmap font generated in code (like the HUD digits), GL_NEAREST
- Typewriter: 1 char / 30 ms; E completes the line instantly, then advances to next line / closes box
- Rendered last, lighting off, depth write off, scissored to the box region

    void hud_dialog_draw(const char* name, const char* line, float type_progress);

## Done when
Text is crisp at native low-res; typewriter respects E-skip; the box never covers the beacon or minimap.

title: PS1 presentation pass: jitter, affine, low-res
description: Sell the era: sub-triangle vertex snapping jitter, affine texture mapping (GL_TEXTURE_MAX_ANISOTROPY off, no perspective correction, non-normalized texture coords), heavy linear fog matched to sky colour, low internal resolution with NEAREST upscale.

title: Buildings: house prefab with doorway anchor
description: Low-poly island house prefab (walls, roof, door, windows) with a doorway anchor point used as the delivery target and a resident NPC slot. Placeable on terrain, aligned to slope.

title: Delivery loop state machine
description:
Sandbox loop with no timer: idle free-roam, pickup package, deliver to the marked resident, award a small score/floating text, then pick a new random recipient. Driving back to the depot is always allowed.

## Design
src/delivery.c/h, stepped on the 60Hz tick (island1-mmap):

    typedef enum { DL_IDLE, DL_CARRYING, DL_DELIVERING } DeliveryPhase;

    typedef struct {
        DeliveryPhase phase;
        int  target_house;     // index into buildings[]
        uint32_t delivered;    // running score
        float deliver_timer;   // DL_DELIVERING countdown
    } DeliveryState;

Transitions:

    DL_IDLE:      near depot (dist < 4 m) AND package available AND input_pressed(ACT_PICKUP)
                  -> spawn parcel on car, pick target house (seeded RNG, reject within 40 m of car), spawn beacon (island1-p3qz), phase = DL_CARRYING
    DL_CARRYING:  dist(car, doorway(target)) < 3.0 AND input_pressed(ACT_DELIVER)
                  -> phase = DL_DELIVERING, deliver_timer = 0.6
    DL_DELIVERING: timer -= dt; at 0 -> delivered++, floating "+1" via island1-5stj,
                  phase = DL_IDLE, parcel despawned; re-pickup at depot allowed immediately

No timer/timeout anywhere — sandbox. Random pick uses the same PRNG family as island1-39q6 for determinism.

Expose for the HUD (island1-n7to): phase, target house id, delivered count; HUD strings: "GO TO DEPOT" / "DELIVER TO HOUSE N" / "DELIVERING...".

## Done when
Full loop pickup -> drive -> deliver -> "+1" -> beacon moves to a new house works end-to-end; re-pickup after delivery is possible; state never dead-ends (IDLE with no package but depot reachable is always valid).

title: On-foot walking animation: leg/arm swing
description:
Drive the leg/arm swing in code from walk speed — PS1-style in-place animation, no skeletal data.

## Design
- Swing = sin(phase) * AMPLITUDE with phase += speed * FREQ * dt (step frequency scales with speed)
- Arms counter-phase legs; amplitude and frequency both go to 0 when idle
- Walk cycle: legs ±35°, arms ∓30°; head bob y = |sin(phase)| * 0.05
- Walking controller (island1-7duk) fills the pose each tick; humanoid_draw applies via glRotatef at pivots
- Later: talking pose (arms crossed) and delivery reaction (one arm raised waving) as named pose targets — lerp swing angles between poses

Geometry stays basic per art direction: box limbs, box head — the swing sells the motion, not the mesh.

## Done when
Standing still -> fully static; walking -> steps in time with speed (no foot slide, <10%); no pop at speed 0; pose targets blend without visible snaps.

title: Chase camera with spring follow and heading lag
Dreamcast render backend (PERFUM + TILE2)
description:
Dreamcast render backend: implement RenderAPI (island1-1dtz) with PERFUM (user-mode vertex pipeline: lighting, HW fog, affine texturing) + TILE2 (hardware sprites) for billboards and 2D.

- PERFUM for meshes (vertex colours, light source, HW fog with the same FrameFog values, affine textures)
- TILE2 for billboards (beacon, prompts, particles) and 2D text/rects
- Bonus later: mirror the HUD onto the VMU screen
Done when: the desktop game's frame renders 1:1 in Kega / NullDC.

title: PSP render backend (GUM + GE)
description:
PSP render backend: implement RenderAPI (island1-1dtz) with GUM (camera/matrices) + GE (vertex submission).

- GUM for view/projection + model matrices; GE DRAW primitives for meshes
- No fixed-function lighting on PSP: rely on baked vertex colours from core meshes (island1-1dtz constraint)
- No hardware fog in GUM/GE -> CPU vertex-colour fog: blend per-vertex colour toward fog colour by distance, using the same FrameFog values as desktop so the look matches
- One texture per mesh, affine mapping, NEAREST; billboards + 2D via GE quads / 2D blits
Done when: the desktop game's frame renders 1:1 on the emulator.

title: Input manager with actions and edge detection

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
History: closed 2026-10-03 (commit b36ab16) when the GLFW input manager + accumulator loop + gfx/passes landed. Reopened: that implementation is GLFW-specific and lives in src/ (core). The description above is the rework target: platform-agnostic contract + per-platform backends.

Migration from current src/input.h: ACT_CONTEXT -> ACT_INTERACT; ACT_RESET -> fly-cam dev key (out of contract); ACT_STEER_L/R -> AX_STEER axis; mouse_dx/dy -> AX_LOOK_X/Y; input_init() (registers GLFW callbacks) -> backend_input_init() in backend/desktop/input_glfw.c; input_axis_steer()/input_axis_throttle() helpers fold into input_axis().

title: Ocean plane with scrolling water texture
description:
Large ocean plane at sea level: scrolling hard-edged water texture with NEAREST sampling, two-layer offset for motion, colour grading toward the horizon and matching fog colour so the plane edge is invisible. Buoyant hover behaviour here is what makes the car read as floating.

## Design
- 300x300 unit quad centered on origin, y = SEA_LEVEL (0.0). Drawn before terrain; depth test on, no blending.
- Texture: hard-edged 64x64 water tile from island1-802h, GL_RGBA, GL_NEAREST, no mipmaps (mip shimmer kills the era look).
- Motion: the GL 1.2/1.5 compat context has NO multi-texture, so the "two-layer offset" becomes one trick: scroll the single layer in world space and tie the rate to the car's velocity — classic PS1 water.

    // world-space scroll, applied to the 4 quad's texture coords
    vec2 s = { car.pos[0] * 0.02f + t * 0.06f, car.pos[2] * 0.02f };
    texcoord = worldcoord * 0.5f + s;      // mod 1.0 in the vertex

  Net effect: water crawls when idle, rushes backwards at speed — no UV animation needed in a shader.
- Color: deep blue-green base (~0.05, 0.32, 0.38) via vertex colors, brighter toward center; the horizon seam disappears because fog color == sky color and fog END lands before the plane edge (see island1-a440).
- Foam/spray from wake is separate (island1-5stj) and renders after this pass.

## Done when
Scrolling freezes when the car stops; no visible plane edge from any camera height or angle; no mip shimmer when the car bobs.

title: Architecture: strict core/backend layering + per-platform build targets
description:
Split the codebase so gameplay/input logic and rendering never mix: core is platform-agnostic C; each platform (desktop now; PSP + Dreamcast later) supplies a thin backend that links in. One codebase compiles to all targets.

## Layout
    src/core/                 # platform-agnostic: input.h (contract), car, delivery,
                              # walking, player, terrain, ocean, dialog, camera math,
                              # mesh data, FrameScene
                              # NO GL/GLFW/PSPLIB/DreamOS headers here
    src/backend/desktop/      # main.c (window + loop), input_glfw.c, render_gl.c
    src/backend/psp/          # main_psp.c, input_psp.c, render_psp.c  (P3, later)
    src/backend/dc/           # main_dc.c,  input_dc.c,  render_dc.c  (P3, later)

## Rules
1. core includes nothing from backend/ and no platform/GL headers
2. One-directional flow: backend polls input -> core ticks -> core produces FrameScene -> backend renders it. Backend never mutates game state; core never calls draw.
3. FrameScene is the only payload crossing the layer: plain data (camera, fog, ordered list of draw items - mesh + transform + tint, billboards, 2D text/rects)
4. main() lives in the backend; core exposes `void game_tick(float dt)` + `const FrameScene* game_frame()`
5. meson: island_core static lib + one executable per platform target (desktop now)
6. Enforcement: a layering check greps core for platform headers/symbols (GL*, GLFW, glad, PSP/KOS, DreamOS/pvr) and must return nothing.

## Done when
Repo matches the layout; the desktop game builds and runs via run.sh/meson; the island_core target builds standalone; the layering check passes.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
Done. Layered layout in place and building clean.

Layout:
- src/core/ = platform-agnostic. render.h/.c (RenderAPI: RenderFrame/RVertex/RDraw, r_frame_begin/clear/camera/fog/vertex/draw), input.h/.c (Action + event injection), camera.h/.c (cglm fly cam), game.h/.c (game_init/resize/tick/render; emits sky + debug grid via r_* only).
- src/backend/desktop/ = GL/GLFW. gfx_gl.{h,c} (fixed-function state manager, default 1x1 white texture, GL_LINEAR fog), render_gl.{h,c} (render_init/shutdown/present; turns r_frame() into gfx/GL calls), input_glfw.{h,c} (GLFW -> input_event_* table), main.c (window + fixed-timestep loop; calls game_tick/game_render and render_present).

Boundary: core includes only core headers + cglm; all GL/GLFW calls live in backend/desktop. Single meson executable('island') over core+backend sources (no separate lib); output unchanged at build/src/island so run.sh path is intact.

Enforcement: scripts/check_layering.sh (comment-stripped grep for GL_*/gl[A-Z]*/glfw/glad/PSP/pspgu/sceGu/KOS/DreamOS/pvr/sgl) wired as meson test 'layering'. `meson test -C build` passes; `meson compile` clean with no warnings; app runs (OpenGL 2.1 compat, fixed-function).

title: Dev loop: git init, gitignore, run script
description: git init the repo, add .gitignore covering build/ build_macos/ subprojects/packagecache/, add a ./run.sh that sets up+compiles and execs the binary, document the meson commands in README. Commit the existing fixed-function scaffold as the baseline.

title: Render pass system with fixed-function state management
description:
Render passes as FrameScene emitters: core emits ordered draw items (sky/ocean/terrain/props/vehicle/particles/beacon/HUD) into the frame; the backend (RenderAPI, see render-abstraction issue) flushes them in order. State (fog, blend, 2D mode) is a flag on the item, not ad-hoc glEnable/glDisable.

## Design
Passes live in core as emitters:

    emit_sky(&frame), emit_ocean(&frame, t), emit_terrain(&frame),
    emit_props(&frame), emit_buildings(&frame), emit_vehicle(&frame, car),
    emit_particles(&frame), emit_beacon(&frame), emit_hud(&frame)

Each appends items with flags (fog on/off, alpha, 2D). The desktop backend diffs its own GL state between items — that's where today's gfx.c state manager goes (backend/desktop, NOT core). 2D/alpha items are self-contained (begin+end their own state), replacing push/pop semantics.

- Removes the ad-hoc glEnable(GL_LIGHTING)/glDisable pairs in render_ground/render_axes (src/render.c:89,125,131,133) into the backend flusher.
- Fog color == sky color so the horizon seam is invisible (island1-a440).

## Done when
No GL state management in core; toggling any single pass out leaves the rest rendering identically (no state bleed); desktop output pixel-identical to pre-refactor.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text: History: closed 2026-10-03 (commit b36ab16) with src/gfx.c (GfxState diffing, push/pop, screen ortho) + src/passes.c (sky gradient + skeleton). Reopened for the layering rework (island1-jimd + island1-1dtz): gfx.c's state diffing moves to backend/desktop as the FrameScene flusher; the passes become FrameScene emitters in core. Desktop output must stay pixel-identical.

title: Collision: terrain height and prop colliders
description: World collision: sample terrain height for ground/air state, circle-vs-circle against prop and building colliders with a bounce/scrub response, keep the car on the ocean plane when over water.

title: Frame loop: fixed-timestep accumulator
Prop scatter system (rocks, palms, clutter)
description: Deterministic scatter of rocks, palms, crates, lamps, fences across island surfaces using a seeded PRNG and terrain slope/height rules. Each prop is low-poly with hard textures; returns a list of colliders for the vehicle.

title: HUD: package status, compass, speed
description: Orthographic overlay pass: package indicator, carried-parcel state, delivered count, speed readout, and a compass/minimap pointing at the active beacon. Rendered after the world with lighting off and depth writes disabled.

title: Shoreline and beach transition
description: Beach ring where terrain crosses sea level: sand blend, wet-sand darkening near the waterline, gentle foam line drawn as geometry or texture band. Visual anchor that reads the island edge.

title: Delivery target beacon
description: Prominent PS1-style beacon at the active recipient's doorway: translucent column or floating holo marker visible above terrain, scaled/alpha-faded with distance so it reads from across the island.

title: Package pickup entity and carry state
description: Spawn a package at a delivery depot on the island; carrying it attaches a parcel mesh to the car and switches HUD state. Picking up again is possible after delivery.

title: Camera collision and above-terrain clamping
description: Raise the chase camera when terrain intrudes between camera and car; clamp camera above terrain/water height so it never clips through the island or dips under the ocean plane.

title: NPC inhabitants with idle and delivery reaction
description:
Low-poly island inhabitants near buildings: blocky humanoid, idle sway, turns to face the player, reaction on delivery. Palette-locked flat colours, no skeletal animation needed.

Uses the shared humanoid mesh from island1-urkr (basic boxes/capsules are fine — head, torso, arms, legs). Per-resident color variants from a small palette table. Idle sway = slow sine on torso/head; delivery reaction = arm-raise wave (pose target from island1-f7at).

title: PSP input backend (pad + analog nub)
description:
PSP controller backend implementing the input contract (island1-ibqg): backend_input_init/poll fills InputState.

Hardware: D-pad (4-way cross, upper-left) . flat sliding analog nub (lower-left, below D-pad) . face buttons Triangle/Circle/Cross/Square . L/R shoulder bumpers . bottom strip: Select, Start, Home, brightness, volume.

Provisional mapping (per island1-ibqg):
  Cross -> ACT_THROTTLE . Circle -> ACT_BRAKE . L -> ACT_BOOST
  Square -> ACT_INTERACT . Triangle -> ACT_VEHICLE
  nub X -> AX_STEER . nub Y -> AX_LOOK_Y (camera pan) . D-pad: steer override when nub in deadzone
  Start -> ACT_PAUSE . Home -> ACT_QUIT
Pad API: pad2 / padReading for digital + analog nub. No mouse - ACT_LOOK stays 0, chase cam only.

Done when: log harness on emulator/dev kit shows correct held/pressed/axis for every button; deadzone verified.

title: Write art-direction spec from reference screenshots
description: The agent cannot read the reference screenshots. Someone must transcribe them into a written art spec: palette (sky/ocean/grass/sand hex values), camera framing and FOV, texture resolution and filtering, fog color/density, silhouette language of car/islands/buildings/NPCs, HUD layout. This spec is the contract for all content tasks (terrain, ocean, car, buildings, textures).

comments.author: hayden
comments.text:
## Reference Image 1 — transcription (provided by user)

Overall: distinctive **PS1-era low-poly retro aesthetic**.

**Foreground & Water**
- Lower half of frame: body of water on textured, low-poly polygonal planes; subtle horizontal ripples; deep blue-green gradients.
- Left side: sharp, blocky splash of white foam erupting from the water surface.

**Vehicle**
- Low-poly red vehicle (retro car / speedboat hybrid) cruising across the water.
- Flat polygonal facets, dark windshield, low profile.

**Midground & Structures**
- Sloping low-poly grassy hill rises against the horizon, dotted with blocky pixelated green trees.
- Near water's edge: rustic wooden dock/structure with small industrial elements — a vertical post and a small tank.

**Background & Sky**
- Bright vibrant blue sky; large stylized chunky white cumulus clouds with blocky pixelated edges.
- Single prominent tree-topped green hill standing tall against the cloudscape.

**UI Overlays** (video-player chrome, likely not part of game art)
- Top corners: playback + audio icons (left); closed captions, options, full-screen icons (right).

Status: provisional art direction input for the spec. Hex palette values, camera FOV/framing, texture resolutions, fog params still TBD.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## Reference Image 2 — transcription (provided by user)

Continues the same **PS1 low-poly retro aesthetic**.

**Foreground & Water Action**
- Camera angle shifts closer to the water's surface.
- Same low-poly red vehicle carving aggressively through choppy blue-green water.
- Large jagged wake of sharp white water plumes and spray erupting directly behind the vehicle — dramatic sense of speed.

**Vehicle**
- Low-poly red car-boat hybrid angled sharply (banking/turning).
- Angular faceted body panels, low wedge profile, dark windshield texture.

**UI Overlays**
- Circular loading/buffering icon overlaid near the front of the vehicle (video-player artifact, not game art).

**Background**

- Bright clear blue sky with a small wispy cloud at the very top.

title: Player character: low-poly humanoid model (shared with residents)
description:
Low-poly blocky humanoid used for both the on-foot player and island residents (island1-r844) — one mesh, different colour schemes.

Basic boxes/capsules only (art direction, user-confirmed) — no sculpted curves; the look comes from flat facets + walk cycle (island1-f7at), not the mesh.

## Design
src/humanoid.c/h, static vertex data in the style of car_mesh.c:

- Head (small box), torso (box), two arms, two legs — separate draw groups so they can pivot in place:
    HUMANOID_BODY, HUMANOID_ARM_L/R, HUMANOID_LEG_L/R
- Pivot at top of arm mesh (shoulder) and top of leg mesh (hip); draw via glPushMatrix/glTranslatef(pivot)/glRotatef(swing)/glPopMatrix
- No shared verts across facets (hard edges, flat normals — PS1 look); vertex colours; player uses the palette primary scheme, residents pull variants from a per-instance colour table
- Size: ~1.7 m tall, 0.5 m shoulder width; origin at feet, +Z facing

    void humanoid_init(void);
    void humanoid_draw(const HumanoidPose* p);   // pose: heading, arm/leg swing angles

## Done when
Standing pose reads blocky-but-human; limb pivots rotate at the right points; the one mesh draws N times with different colours; hard facets visible under GL_LIGHT0.

title: Terrain mesh and texturing
description: Terrain mesh textured per surface type (grass/sand/rock) with hard texture-env blends and visible triangle edges, matching the spec palette. Use client-state vertex arrays (glVertexPointer/glTexCoordPointer/glColorPointer) + glDrawArrays, not VBOs.

title: Player mode state machine: on-foot/in-vehicle, entering and exiting
description:
Toggle between on-foot and in-vehicle. Car stays parked where you exit. Carried package transfers between modes.

## Design
src/player.c/h:

    typedef enum { MODE_ON_FOOT, MODE_IN_VEHICLE } PlayerMode;

    typedef struct {
        PlayerMode mode;
        vec3  pos; float heading;   // on-foot state
        float transition_t;         // 0.5 s crossfade
    } Player;
    // vehicle state lives in CarState (island1-9n0n)

Entering:
    near a car (dist < 3.0 m) AND |car.speed| < 1.0 m/s AND press ACT_BOARD
    -> hide humanoid, mode = IN_VEHICLE, camera blends to vehicle framing

Exiting:
    in vehicle AND |car.speed| < 1.0 m/s AND press ACT_EXIT
    -> place player beside car (car right vector * 1.2 m), mode = ON_FOOT,
       car stays put (vel = 0, no idle drift)

- Add ACT_BOARD/ACT_EXIT to input actions (island1-ibqg); both bound to F as one context key
- Carried package moves with the player; delivery target is not reset on mode switch (island1-draq)
- On-foot camera: reuse chase cam (island1-fnss) with distance 4.5 / height 1.9 (vs 7.0/3.2 in vehicle); lerp params during transition_t

## Done when
Enter/exit works anywhere (land or water) when stopped; no flicker between body and car during transition; on-foot camera framing matches PS1 references; carried package and target persist across the switch.
